Session 2 finding: Age differs strongly by class (Kruskal-Wallis; nevi from young patients)
Still true on the full dataset?: yes: median age NV 40 vs BCC 65, SCCKA 70
Consequence for the pipeline: age is NOT an input of the image pipeline; stratified splits keep the age mix similar; check later that the model does not just learn 'young skin = benign'

Session 2 finding: Six columns leak the label (diagnosis_2/3/4, melanocytic, diagnosis_confirm_type, concomitant_biopsy)
Consequence for the pipeline: excluded from model inputs; the split CSVs carry only ids, image_type and the labels

Session 2 finding: image_manipulation = 'altered' is enriched in Indeterminate lesions
Consequence for the pipeline: possible acquisition shortcut: not an input; report metrics separately for altered images

Session 2 finding: Colour alone separates Malignant from Benign only weakly (sample AUC <= 0.66)
Still true on the full dataset?: yes, on all 10,480 images: best single-feature AUC 0.67
Consequence for the pipeline: a CNN must learn spatial patterns; colour augmentation stays mild (no hue jitter)

Session 2 finding: Dermoscopic images are much bluer than clinical ones (device effect > class effect)
Consequence for the pipeline: both images of a lesion go to the same split, so every split has both types in equal numbers; evaluate per image type as well

Session 2 finding: A missing body site goes with more Benign lesions
Still true on the full dataset?: yes: 34.5% Benign when missing vs 28.3% overall; explained: 3,850 of the 3,912 'missing' images are trunk lesions in training_input.csv
Consequence for the pipeline: missing is not random: if site is used, recover 'trunk' from training_input.csv, the rest 'unknown'
